<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt 15pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:36pt;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt 15pt;text-align:justify;"><b>Long-Lived Assets</b></p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt 15pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:36pt;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt 15pt;text-align:justify;">The Company&rsquo;s management assesses the recoverability of long-lived assets (other than goodwill discussed above) upon the occurrence of a triggering event by determining whether the carrying value of long-lived assets can be recovered through projected undiscounted future cash flows over&nbsp;their remaining useful lives. The amount of long-lived asset impairment, if any, is measured based on fair value and is charged to operations in the period in which long-lived asset impairment is determined by management. At <em data-td-invalid-detail="1" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;"> June 30, 2018, </em>the Company&rsquo;s management believes there is <em data-td-fact-id="34616527" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">no</em> impairment of its long-lived assets. There can be <em data-td-fact-id="34616528" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">no</em> assurance, however, that market conditions will <em data-td-fact-id="34616529" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">not</em> change or demand for the Company&rsquo;s products and services will continue, which could result in impairment of long-lived assets in the future.</p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt 15pt;text-align:center;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt 7.5pt;text-align:center;">F-<em data-td-fact-id="34616530" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">10</em></p>

<div data-thunderdome-xbrl-exclude="1" id="PGBK" style="width: 100%; margin-left: 0pt; margin-right: 0pt">
<div id="PGNUM" style="text-align: center; width: 100%">&nbsp;</div>

</div>

<p style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt 7.5pt;text-align:left;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt 7.5pt;text-align:left;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt 15pt;text-align:justify;"><b>Debt Issuance Costs</b></p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt 15pt;text-align:justify;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt 15pt;text-align:justify;">Debt issuance costs represent costs incurred in connection with the issuance of long-term debt.&nbsp; Debt issuance costs are amortized over the term of the financing instrument using the effective interest method.&nbsp; Debt issuance costs are presented in the&nbsp;consolidated balance sheets&nbsp;as an offset against the current and non-current portions of long-term debt.</p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt 15pt;text-align:justify;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt 15pt;text-align:justify;"><b>Issuance of Equity Instruments to Non-Employees</b></p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt 15pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:36pt;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt 15pt;text-align:justify;">All issuances of the Company&rsquo;s equity instruments to non-employees are measured at fair value based upon either the fair value of the equity instruments issued or the fair value of consideration received, whichever is more readily determinable. The majority of stock issuances for non-cash consideration pertains to services rendered by consultants and others and has been valued at the fair value of the equity instruments on the dates issued.</p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt 15pt;text-align:justify;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt 15pt;text-align:justify;">The measurement date for the fair value of the equity instruments issued is determined at the earlier of (i) the date at which a commitment for performance by the consultant or vendor is reached or (ii) the date at which the consultant or vendor&rsquo;s performance is complete. In the case of equity instruments issued to consultants, the fair value of the equity instrument is recognized over the term of the consulting agreement.&nbsp;&nbsp;Assets acquired in exchange for the issuance of fully vested, non-forfeitable equity instruments are <em data-td-fact-id="34616531" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">not</em> presented or classified as an offset to equity on the grantor&rsquo;s balance sheet once the equity instrument is granted for accounting purposes. &nbsp;</p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt 15pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:36pt;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt 15pt;text-align:justify;"><b>Stock-Based Compensation</b></p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt 15pt;text-align:justify;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt 15pt;text-align:justify;">The Company accounts for stock-based compensation under the provisions of ASC <em data-td-fact-id="34616532" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">No.</em> <em data-td-fact-id="34616533" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">718,</em><i> Compensation - Stock Compensation</i> (&ldquo;ASC <em data-td-fact-id="34616534" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">718&rdquo;</em>). ASC <em data-td-fact-id="34616535" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">718</em> requires the recognition of the fair value of the stock-based compensation in net income. Compensation expense associated with market-based restricted stock is determined using a Monte-Carlo valuation model, and compensation expense associated with time-based restricted stock is determined based on the number of shares granted and the fair value on the date of grant. For valuing stock options awards, the Company has elected to use the Black-Scholes model. For the expected term, the Company uses a simple average of the vesting period and the contractual term of the option. Volatility is a measure of the amount by which the Company&rsquo;s stock price is expected to fluctuate during the expected term of the option. For volatility the Company considers its own volatility as applicable for valuing its options and warrants. With the adoption of ASU <em data-td-fact-id="34616536" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">2016</em>-<em data-td-fact-id="34616537" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">09</em> during the year ended <em data-td-invalid-detail="1" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;"> June 30, 2017, </em>forfeitures are&nbsp;accounted&nbsp;for as they are incurred, rather than estimated at time of grant. The risk-free interest rate is based on the relevant&nbsp;US Treasury Bill Rate at the time of each grant. The dividend yield represents the dividend rate expected to be paid over the option&rsquo;s expected term; the Company currently has <em data-td-fact-id="34616538" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">no</em> plans to pay dividends.&nbsp; The fair value of stock-based awards is amortized over the vesting period of the award or expected vesting date of the market-based restricted shares&nbsp;and the Company elected to use the straight-line method for awards granted.</p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt 15pt;text-align:justify;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt 15pt;text-align:justify;"><b>Revenue Recognition</b></p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt 15pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:36pt;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt 15pt;text-align:justify;">Software license revenue is recognized when persuasive evidence of an arrangement exists, delivery of the product component has occurred, the fee is fixed and determinable, and collectability is reasonably assured. If any of these criteria are <em data-td-fact-id="34616539" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">not</em> met, revenue recognition is deferred until such time as all of the criteria are met.</p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt 15pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:36pt;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt 15pt;text-align:justify;">The Company accounts for delivered elements in accordance with the selling price when arrangements include multiple product components or other elements and vendor-specific objective evidence exists for the value of all undelivered elements. Revenues on undelivered elements are recognized once delivery is complete.</p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt 15pt;text-align:justify;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt 15pt;text-align:justify;">In those instances, in which arrangements include significant customization, contractual milestones, acceptance criteria or other contingencies, the Company accounts for the arrangements&nbsp;using contract accounting, as follows:</p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt 15pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:36pt;">&nbsp;</p>

<table border="0" cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" style="margin-left:1.4%;width:98%;text-indent:0;font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;">

		<tr style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">
			<td style="vertical-align: top; width: 7.4%; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">
			<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:0pt;margin-right:0.8pt;margin-top:0pt;text-align:center;">&bull;</p>
			</td>
			<td style="vertical-align: top; width: 92.6%; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">
			<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:0pt;margin-right:0.8pt;margin-top:0pt;text-align:justify;">when customer acceptance can be estimated, but reliable estimated costs to complete cannot be determined, expenditures are capitalized as work-in process and deferred until completion of the contract at which time the costs and revenues are recognized.</p>
			</td>
		</tr>
		<tr style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">

			<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:0pt;margin-right:0.8pt;margin-top:0pt;text-align:center;">&bull;</p>
			</td>
			<td style="vertical-align: top; width: 92.6%; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">
			<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:0pt;margin-right:0.8pt;margin-top:0pt;text-align:justify;">when customer acceptance cannot be estimated based on historical evidence, costs are expensed as incurred and revenue is recognized at the completion of the contract when customer acceptance is obtained.</p>
			</td>
		</tr>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt 15pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:36pt;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt 15pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:36pt;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt 15pt;text-align:justify;">The Company records amounts collected from customers in excess of recognizable revenue as deferred revenue in the accompanying consolidated balance sheets. Revenues for maintenance agreements, software support, online services and information products are recognized ratably over the term of the service agreement.</p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt 15pt;text-align:justify;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt 7.5pt;text-align:center;">F-<em data-td-fact-id="34616540" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">11</em></p>

<div data-thunderdome-xbrl-exclude="1" id="PGBK" style="width: 100%; margin-left: 0pt; margin-right: 0pt">
<div id="PGNUM" style="text-align: center; width: 100%">&nbsp;</div>

<div id="PGHDR" style="text-align: left; width: 100%">&nbsp;</div>
</div>

<p style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt 7.5pt;text-align:left;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt 7.5pt;text-align:left;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt 15pt;text-align:justify;">The Company recognizes revenue on a net basis, which excludes sales tax collected from customers and remitted to governmental authorities.</p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt 15pt;text-align:justify;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt 15pt;text-align:justify;"><b>Cost of Revenues </b></p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:16.5pt;margin-right:7.5pt;margin-top:0pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:24pt;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:16.5pt;margin-right:7.5pt;margin-top:0pt;text-align:justify;">Cost of revenues primarily consists of expenses related to delivering our service and providing support, amortization expense associated with capitalized software related to our services and acquired developed technologies and certain fees paid to various <em data-td-fact-id="34616541" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">third</em> parties for the use of their technology, services and data. Included in costs of revenues are cost of professional services, which consists primarily of employee-related costs associated with these services, the cost of subcontractors, certain <em data-td-fact-id="34616542" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">third</em>-party fees, and allocated overhead.</p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:16.5pt;margin-right:7.5pt;margin-top:0pt;text-align:justify;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:16.5pt;margin-right:7.5pt;margin-top:0pt;text-align:justify;">As we continue to invest in new products and services, the amortization expense associated with these capitalizable activities will be included in cost of revenues. Additionally, as we enter into new contracts with <em data-td-fact-id="34616543" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">third</em> parties for the use of their technology, services or data, or as our sales volume grows, the fees paid to use such technology or services <em data-td-invalid-detail="1" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;"> may </em>increase. The timing of these additional expenses will affect our cost of revenues, both in terms of absolute dollars and as a percentage of revenues, in the affected periods.</p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt 15pt;text-align:justify;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt 15pt;text-align:justify;"><b>Advertising Expense</b></p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt 15pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:36pt;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt 15pt;text-align:justify;">The Company expenses advertising costs as incurred. For the years ended <em data-td-invalid-detail="1" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;"> June 30, 2018 </em>and <em data-td-fact-id="34616544" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">2017,</em> advertising expense totaled <em data-td-fact-id="34616545" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">$0.4</em> million&nbsp;and <em data-td-fact-id="34616546" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">$0.4</em> million, respectively.</p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt 15pt;text-align:justify;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt 15pt;text-align:justify;"><b>Foreign Currency</b></p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt 15pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:36pt;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt 15pt;text-align:justify;">Management has determined that the functional currency of its subsidiaries is the local currency. Assets and liabilities of the&nbsp;UK subsidiaries are translated into&nbsp;US dollars at the year-end exchange rates. Income and expenses are translated at an average exchange rate for the year and the resulting translation gain (loss) adjustments are accumulated as a separate component of stockholders&rsquo; equity. The translation gain (loss) adjustment totaled <em data-td-fact-id="34616547" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">$47,000</em> and&nbsp;$(<em data-td-fact-id="34616548" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">0.3</em>) million&nbsp;for the years ended <em data-td-invalid-detail="1" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;"> June 30, 2018 </em>and <em data-td-fact-id="34616549" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">2017,</em> respectively.</p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt 15pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:36pt;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt 15pt;text-align:justify;">Foreign currency gains and losses from transactions denominated in other than respective local currencies are included in income. The Company had <em data-td-fact-id="34616550" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">no</em> material foreign currency transaction gains (losses) for all periods presented.</p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt 15pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:36pt;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt 15pt;text-align:justify;"><b>Comprehensive Income</b></p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt 15pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:36pt;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt 15pt;text-align:justify;">Comprehensive income includes all changes in equity (net assets) during a period from non-owner sources. For the years ended <em data-td-invalid-detail="1" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;"> June 30, 2018 </em>and <em data-td-fact-id="34616551" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">2017,</em> the components of comprehensive income consist of foreign currency translation gains (losses).</p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt 15pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:36pt;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt 15pt;text-align:justify;"><b>Income Taxes</b></p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt 15pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:36pt;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt 15.1pt; text-align: justify;">Deferred tax assets and liabilities are recognized for the future tax consequences attributable to differences between the financial statement carrying amounts of existing assets and liabilities and their respective tax bases. Deferred tax assets and liabilities are measured using enacted tax rates expected to apply to taxable income in the years in which those temporary differences are expected to be recovered or settled. The effect on deferred tax assets and liabilities of a change in tax rates is recognized in income in the period the enactment occurs. Deferred taxation is provided in full in respect of timing differences between the treatment of certain items for taxation and accounting purposes. Valuation allowances are established, when necessary, to reduce deferred tax assets to the amount expected to be realized.</p>

<p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt 15.1pt; text-align: justify;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt 15.1pt; text-align: justify;">The calculation of the Company&rsquo;s tax liabilities involves dealing with uncertainties in the application of complex tax laws and regulations. ASC&nbsp;<em data-td-fact-id="34616552" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">740</em>&nbsp;states that a tax benefit from an uncertain tax position&nbsp;<em data-td-invalid-detail="1" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;"> may&nbsp;</em>be recognized when it is more likely than&nbsp;<em data-td-fact-id="34616553" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">not</em>&nbsp;that the position will be sustained upon examination on the basis of the technical merits. The Company records unrecognized tax benefits as liabilities in accordance with ASC&nbsp;<em data-td-fact-id="34616554" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">740</em>&nbsp;and adjusts these liabilities based on new information&nbsp;<em data-td-fact-id="34616555" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">not</em>&nbsp;previously available. Because of the complexity of some of these uncertainties, the ultimate resolution&nbsp;<em data-td-invalid-detail="1" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;"> may&nbsp;</em>result in a payment that is materially different from our current estimate of the unrecognized tax benefit liabilities. As of <em data-td-invalid-detail="1" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;"> June 30, 2018,&nbsp;</em>the Company accrued unrecognized tax benefits totaling&nbsp;<em data-td-fact-id="34616556" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">$0.2</em>&nbsp;million.</p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt 15.1pt;text-align:justify;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt 15.1pt;text-align:justify;">The Company&rsquo;s practice is to recognize interest and/or penalties related to income tax matters in income tax expense.&nbsp;</p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt 15pt;text-align:justify;"><b>&nbsp;</b></p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt 15pt;text-align:justify;"><b>Basic and Diluted Earnings Per Share</b></p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt 15pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:36pt;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt 15.1pt;text-align:justify;">Basic earnings per share (&ldquo;BEPS&rdquo;) is computed by dividing the net income by the weighted average number of common shares outstanding for the period. Diluted earnings per share (&ldquo;DEPS&rdquo;) is computed giving effect to all dilutive potential common shares outstanding during the period. Dilutive potential common shares consist of incremental shares issuable upon the exercise of stock options and warrants using the &ldquo;treasury stock&rdquo; method. The computation of DEPS does <em data-td-fact-id="34616557" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">not</em> assume conversion, exercise or contingent exercise of securities that would have an anti-dilutive effect on earnings. For the years ended&nbsp;<em data-td-invalid-detail="1" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;"> June 30, 2018&nbsp;</em>and <em data-td-fact-id="34616558" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">2017</em>&nbsp;there were&nbsp;common share equivalents of <em data-td-fact-id="34616559" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">56,626</em> and <em data-td-fact-id="34616560" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">54,008,</em> respectively, included in the computation of the DEPS. For the years ended <em data-td-invalid-detail="1" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;"> June 30, 2018 </em>and <em data-td-fact-id="34616561" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">2017,</em>&nbsp;<em data-td-fact-id="34616562" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">450,178</em> and <em data-td-fact-id="34616563" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">503,951</em> shares of common stock, respectively, vest based on the market price of the Company&rsquo;s common stock and were excluded from the computation of DEPS because the shares have <em data-td-fact-id="34616564" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">not</em> vested, but <em data-td-fact-id="34616565" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">no</em> stock options were excluded from the computation of DEPS.</p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:7.5pt;margin-right:15pt;margin-top:0pt;text-align:center;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt 7.5pt;text-align:center;">F-<em data-td-fact-id="34616566" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">12</em></p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt 15pt;text-align:left;"><b>&nbsp;</b></p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:0pt;margin-right:7.5pt;margin-top:0pt;text-align:justify;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt 15pt;text-align:justify;"><b>&nbsp;</b></p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:18pt;margin-right:31pt;margin-top:0pt;text-align:left;"><b>Reclassifications</b></p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:18pt;margin-right:31pt;margin-top:0pt;text-align:left;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:18pt;margin-right:31pt;margin-top:0pt;text-align:justify;">Certain assets were reclassified from inventories&nbsp;to&nbsp;other current assets and other long-term assets&nbsp;and reclassified from other current assets to accounts receivable&nbsp;and certain liabilities&nbsp;were reclassified from accrued expenses to accrued payroll&nbsp;and related expenses and deferred revenues, net of current portion, as of&nbsp;<em data-td-invalid-detail="1" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;"> June 30, 2017&nbsp;</em>in order to conform to the current period presentation in the accompanying&nbsp;consolidated balance sheets and cash flows with&nbsp;<em data-td-fact-id="34616567" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">no</em>&nbsp;net effect on the previously reported net income.</p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt 15pt;text-align:justify;"><b>&nbsp;</b></p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt 15pt;text-align:justify;"><b>&nbsp;</b></p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:7.5pt;margin-right:15pt;margin-top:0pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:7.5pt;"><b>Recent Accounting Pronouncements</b></p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt 15pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:36pt;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:13.5pt;margin-right:22.5pt;margin-top:0pt;text-align:justify;">&nbsp;<i>Recently Adopted Accounting Standards</i></p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:13.5pt;margin-right:22.5pt;margin-top:0pt;text-align:justify;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:13.5pt;margin-right:22.5pt;margin-top:0pt;text-align:justify;">In&nbsp;<em data-td-invalid-detail="1" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;"> August 2016,&nbsp;</em>the FASB issued ASU&nbsp;<em data-td-fact-id="34616568" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">2016</em>-<em data-td-fact-id="34616569" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">15,</em>&nbsp;<i>Statement of Cash Flows (Topic&nbsp;</i><em data-td-fact-id="34616570" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">230</em><i>), Classification of Certain Cash Receipts and Cash Payments</i>. The Company did&nbsp;<em data-td-fact-id="34616571" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">not</em>&nbsp;have additional disclosures or changes in cash flow presentation in its consolidated financial statements as a result of the adoption of&nbsp;this standard on&nbsp;<em data-td-invalid-detail="1" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;"> July 1, 2017.</em></p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:13.5pt;margin-right:22.5pt;margin-top:0pt;text-align:justify;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:13.5pt;margin-right:22.5pt;margin-top:0pt;text-align:justify;">In&nbsp;<em data-td-invalid-detail="1" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;"> August 2014,&nbsp;</em>the FASB issued ASU&nbsp;<em data-td-fact-id="34616572" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">2014</em>-<em data-td-fact-id="34616573" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">15,</em>&nbsp;<i>Presentation of Financial Statements-Going Concern</i>.&nbsp;Currently, there is&nbsp;<em data-td-fact-id="34616574" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">no</em>&nbsp;guidance in accounting principles generally accepted in the US about management&rsquo;s responsibility to evaluate whether there is substantial doubt about an entity&rsquo;s ability to continue as a going concern or to provide related footnote disclosures. The update requires management to assess the Company&rsquo;s ability to continue as a going concern by incorporating and expanding upon certain US accounting principles. Specifically, the amendments in the update (<em data-td-fact-id="34616575" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">1</em>) provide a definition of the term &quot;substantial doubt,&quot; (<em data-td-fact-id="34616576" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">2</em>) require an evaluation every reporting period (including interim periods), (<em data-td-fact-id="34616577" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">3</em>) provide principles for considering the mitigating effect of management&rsquo;s plans, (<em data-td-fact-id="34616578" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">4</em>) require certain disclosures when substantial doubt is alleviated as a result of consideration of management&rsquo;s plans, (<em data-td-fact-id="34616579" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">5</em>) require an express statement and other disclosures when substantial doubt is&nbsp;<em data-td-fact-id="34616580" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">not</em>&nbsp;alleviated, and (<em data-td-fact-id="34616581" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">6</em>) require an assessment for a period of&nbsp;<em data-td-fact-id="34616582" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">one</em>&nbsp;year after the date that the financial statements are issued (or available to be issued).&nbsp; Based on the Company&#39;s evaluation as of <em data-td-invalid-detail="1" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;"> June 30,&nbsp;</em><em data-td-fact-id="34616583" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">2018,</em>&nbsp;there is&nbsp;<em data-td-fact-id="34616584" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">not</em>&nbsp;substantial doubt about the Company&#39;s ability to continue as a going concern and&nbsp;<em data-td-fact-id="34616585" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">no</em>&nbsp;additional disclosures are required at this time.</p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt 15pt;text-align:justify;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt 15pt;text-align:justify;"><i>&nbsp;</i></p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt 15pt;text-align:justify;"><i>&nbsp;</i></p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt 15pt;text-align:justify;"><i>&nbsp;</i></p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt 15pt;text-align:justify;"><i>&nbsp;</i></p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt 15pt;text-align:justify;"><i>&nbsp;</i></p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt 15pt;text-align:center;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt 15pt;text-align:center;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt 7.5pt;text-align:center;">F-<em data-td-fact-id="34616586" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">13</em></p>

<div data-thunderdome-xbrl-exclude="1" id="PGBK" style="width: 100%; margin-left: 0pt; margin-right: 0pt">
<div id="PGNUM" style="text-align: center; width: 100%">&nbsp;</div>

<hr style="PAGE-BREAK-AFTER: always; border: none; width: 100%; height: 2px; color: #000000; background-color: #000000">
<div id="PGHDR" style="text-align: left; width: 100%">&nbsp;</div>
</div>

<p style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt 7.5pt;text-align:left;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt 7.5pt;text-align:left;"><i>&nbsp;</i></p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt 15pt;text-align:justify;"><i>&nbsp;Accounting Standards <em data-td-fact-id="34616587" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">Not</em> Yet Adopted</i></p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt 15pt;text-align:justify;"><i>&nbsp;</i></p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt 15pt;text-align:justify;">In <em data-td-invalid-detail="1" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;"> May 2017, </em>the FASB issued ASU <em data-td-fact-id="34616588" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">2017</em>-<em data-td-fact-id="34616589" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">09,</em>&nbsp;<i>Compensation - Stock Compensation (Topic <em data-td-fact-id="34616590" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">718</em>): Scope of Modification Accounting</i>, which provides guidance about which changes to the terms or conditions of a share-based payment award require an entity to apply modification accounting in ASC Topic <em data-td-fact-id="34616591" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">718.</em> Under the new guidance, modification accounting is required only if the fair value, the vesting conditions, or the classification of the award (as equity or liability) changes as a result of the change in terms or conditions.&nbsp;ASU&nbsp;<em data-td-fact-id="34616592" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">2017</em>-<em data-td-fact-id="34616593" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">09</em>&nbsp;will be effective for the Company for the fiscal year ending&nbsp;<em data-td-invalid-detail="1" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">June 30, 2019 </em>and interim reporting periods within that year. Early adoption is permitted. The Company expects the adoption of this guidance will <em data-td-fact-id="34616594" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">not</em> have a material effect on the Company&rsquo;s consolidated financial statements.</p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt 15pt;text-align:justify;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt 15pt;text-align:justify;">In <em data-td-invalid-detail="1" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;"> January 2017, </em>the FASB issued&nbsp;ASU <em data-td-fact-id="34616595" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">2017</em>-<em data-td-fact-id="34616596" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">04,</em>&nbsp;<i>Intangibles-Goodwill and Other (Topic <em data-td-fact-id="34616597" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">350</em>): Simplifying the Test for Goodwill Impairment</i>. This update simplifies the subsequent measurement of goodwill by eliminating step <em data-td-fact-id="34616598" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">two</em> from the goodwill impairment test. Under the new guidance, an entity performs its annual, or interim, goodwill impairment test by comparing the fair value of a reporting unit with its carrying amount and recognizes an impairment charge for the amount by which the carrying amount exceeds the reporting unit&rsquo;s fair value, <em data-td-fact-id="34616599" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">not</em> to exceed the carrying amount of goodwill allocated to the reporting unit. ASU <em data-td-fact-id="34616600" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">2017</em>-<em data-td-fact-id="34616601" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">04</em> will be effective for the Company for the fiscal year ending&nbsp;<em data-td-invalid-detail="1" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">June 30, 2021. </em>Early adoption is permitted.&nbsp;The&nbsp;Company does <em data-td-fact-id="34616602" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">not</em> expect the adoption of ASU <em data-td-fact-id="34616603" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">2017</em>-<em data-td-fact-id="34616604" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">04</em> to have a significant impact on its consolidated financial statements.&nbsp;</p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt 15pt;text-align:justify;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt 15pt;text-align:justify;">In <em data-td-invalid-detail="1" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;"> February 2016, </em>the FASB issued ASU <em data-td-fact-id="34616605" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">2016</em>-<em data-td-fact-id="34616606" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">02,</em> <i>Leases</i>. The update requires lessees to present right-of-use assets and lease liabilities on the balance sheet for all leases with terms longer than <em data-td-fact-id="34616607" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">12</em> months. The guidance is to be applied using a modified retrospective approach at the beginning of the earliest comparative period in the financial statements and will be effective for the Company for the fiscal year ending&nbsp;<em data-td-invalid-detail="1" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">June 30, 2021. </em>The Company is currently assessing the impact the adoption of ASU <em data-td-fact-id="34616608" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">2016</em>-<em data-td-fact-id="34616609" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">02</em> will have on its consolidated financial statements.</p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt 15pt;text-align:justify;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt 15pt;text-align:justify;">In <em data-td-invalid-detail="1" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;"> May 2014, </em>the FASB issued ASU <em data-td-fact-id="34616610" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">2014</em>-<em data-td-fact-id="34616611" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">09</em><i>, Revenue from Contracts with Customers </i>(Topic <em data-td-fact-id="34616612" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">606</em>), which amends the existing accounting standards for revenue recognition. ASU <em data-td-fact-id="34616613" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">2014</em>-<em data-td-fact-id="34616614" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">09</em> is based on principles that govern the recognition of revenue at an amount an entity expects to be entitled when products are transferred to customers. In <em data-td-invalid-detail="1" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;"> July&nbsp;</em><em data-td-fact-id="34616615" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">2015,</em> the FASB provided a <em data-td-fact-id="34616616" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">one</em>-year delay in the effective date of ASU <em data-td-fact-id="34616617" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">2014</em>-<em data-td-fact-id="34616618" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">09,</em> to be effective for annual reporting periods beginning after <em data-td-invalid-detail="1" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;"> December&nbsp;</em><em data-td-fact-id="34616619" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">15,</em> <em data-td-fact-id="34616620" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">2017,</em> including interim periods within that reporting period, and a permission to early adopt for annual and interim periods beginning after <em data-td-invalid-detail="1" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;"> December&nbsp;</em><em data-td-fact-id="34616621" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">15,</em> <em data-td-fact-id="34616622" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">2016.</em> &nbsp;&nbsp;The Company has performed a review of the new revenue standard and is monitoring the activity of the FASB and the transition resource group as it relates to specific interpretative guidance. The Company plans to adopt ASU <em data-td-fact-id="34616623" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">2014</em>-<em data-td-fact-id="34616624" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">09</em> on <em data-td-invalid-detail="1" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;"> July 1, 2018. </em>The Company has&nbsp;<em data-td-fact-id="34616625" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">not</em>&nbsp;yet determined whether it will adopt the provisions of ASU&nbsp;<em data-td-fact-id="34616626" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">2014</em>-<em data-td-fact-id="34616627" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">09</em>&nbsp;on a retrospective basis or through a cumulative adjustment to retained earnings.&nbsp;The new standard could change the amount and timing of revenue and costs under certain arrangement types and could increase the administrative burden on Company operations to properly account for customer contracts and provide the more expansive required disclosures. The Company is currently completing its review of contracts, and therefore has <em data-td-fact-id="34616628" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">not</em> completed its quantification yet to know the impact the adoption will have on its consolidated financial position, results of operation or cash flows.</p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt 15pt;text-align:left;"><b>NOTE </b><b><em data-td-fact-id="34616634" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">3</em></b><b>. INTANGIBLE ASSETS</b></p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt 15pt;text-align:left;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt 15pt;text-align:justify;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt 16.5pt;text-align:justify;">On <em data-td-invalid-detail="1" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;"> March 2, 2017, </em>the Company entered into a credit facility (&quot;Credit Facility&quot;) with Univest Bank and Trust Co. (&ldquo;Univest&rdquo;). &nbsp;In connection with the Credit Facility, the parties entered into ancillary agreements,&nbsp;including a credit agreement, a revolving credit note and a term note (collectively, the &quot;Credit Agreements&quot;). The Credit Facility allows for borrowings up to <em data-td-fact-id="34616641" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">$11.5</em> million consisting of an <em data-td-fact-id="34616642" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">$8.75</em> million term loan and a <em data-td-fact-id="34616643" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">$2.75</em> million revolver. &nbsp;The Company used the initial proceeds of the Credit Facility to repay all of its obligations under its prior credit facility. The borrowings under the Credit Agreements bear interest at a variable rate based on either LIBO Rate (as defined in the Credit Agreements) or the Univest Float Rate&nbsp;(as defined in the Credit Agreements), plus an applicable margin of <em data-td-fact-id="34616644" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">2.75%</em> to <em data-td-fact-id="34616645" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">3.25%,</em> based upon financial covenants.&nbsp; The term note requires monthly payments of <em data-td-fact-id="34616646" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">$133,333</em> through <em data-td-invalid-detail="1" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;"> December 1, 2017, </em>then <em data-td-fact-id="34616647" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">$158,333</em> through <em data-td-invalid-detail="1" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;"> December 1, 2018, </em>and <em data-td-fact-id="34616648" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">$175,000</em> thereafter through maturity. The maturity date under the Credit Agreements is <em data-td-invalid-detail="1" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;"> August 1, 2021.</em></p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt 15pt;text-align:left;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt 15pt;text-align:justify;">As of <em data-td-invalid-detail="1" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;"> June 30, 2018, </em>the Company did <em data-td-fact-id="34616649" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">not</em> have any borrowings under its revolving credit note.&nbsp; Under the terms of the Credit&nbsp;Agreements, the Company is required to comply with certain loan covenants, which include, but are <em data-td-fact-id="34616650" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">not</em> limited to, the maintenance of certain financial ratios as well as certain financial reporting requirements and limitations. The Company&rsquo;s obligations under the Credit Agreements are secured by all of the Company&rsquo;s US assets and are guaranteed by the Company&rsquo;s US wholly-owned subsidiary, MAM Software Inc.&nbsp; Additionally, the Company pledged <em data-td-fact-id="34616651" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">65%</em> of the stock of MAM Software Limited, its UK subsidiary.&nbsp; As of <em data-td-invalid-detail="1" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;"> June 30, 2018, </em>the Company was in compliance with its loan covenants.</p>

<div contenteditable="false" docsect="9" id="30967" sectdesc="Note to Financial Statements">&nbsp;</div>

<div data-td-parse-id="1" data-td-statement-type="note" data-td-v2v-id="1536262809419" id="thunderdome-statement-994312">
<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt 15pt;text-align:justify;"><b>NOTE </b><b><em data-td-fact-id="34616652" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">5</em></b><b>. INCOME TAXES</b></p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt 15pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:36pt;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt 15pt;text-align:justify;">The Company is subject to taxation in the US,&nbsp;UK and various&nbsp;US state jurisdictions. The Company&rsquo;s tax years for <em data-td-fact-id="34616653" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">1999</em> and forward are subject to examination by the&nbsp;US and state tax authorities due to losses incurred since inception. The Company is currently <em data-td-fact-id="34616654" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">not</em> under any material examination by any taxing authorities.</p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt 15pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:36pt;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt 15pt;text-align:justify;">The Company follows the provisions of ASC <em data-td-fact-id="34616655" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">740</em>-<em data-td-fact-id="34616656" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">10,</em> <i>Income Taxes</i>, that defines a recognition threshold and measurement attributes for the financial recognition and measurement of a tax position taken or expected to be taken in a tax return. ASC <em data-td-fact-id="34616657" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">740</em>-<em data-td-fact-id="34616658" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">10</em>&nbsp;also provides guidance on the de-recognition, classification, interest and penalties, accounting in interim periods, disclosure, and transition. Under ASC <em data-td-fact-id="34616659" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">740</em>-<em data-td-fact-id="34616660" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">10,</em> the impact of an uncertain income tax position on the income tax return must be recognized at the largest amount that is more-likely-than-<em data-td-fact-id="34616661" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">not</em> to be sustained upon audit by the relevant taxing authority. An uncertain income tax position will <em data-td-fact-id="34616662" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">not</em> be recognized if it has less than a&nbsp;<em data-td-fact-id="34616663" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">50%</em> likelihood&nbsp;of being sustained.</p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt 15pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:36pt;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt 15pt;text-align:justify;">The Company has <em data-td-fact-id="34616664" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">$0.2</em> million of&nbsp;unrecognized tax benefits that, if recognized, would affect the effective tax rate.</p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt 15pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:36pt;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt 15pt;text-align:justify;">The Company&rsquo;s practice is to recognize interest and/or penalties related to income matters in income tax expense. During the&nbsp;year ended <em data-td-invalid-detail="1" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;"> June 30, 2017, </em>the Company recognized penalties of <em data-td-fact-id="34616665" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">$0.1</em> million. The Company did <em data-td-fact-id="34616666" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">not</em> recognize any penalties for the year ended <em data-td-invalid-detail="1" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;"> June 30, 2018.&nbsp;&nbsp;</em></p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt 15pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:36pt;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt 16.5pt;text-align:justify;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt 16.5pt;text-align:justify;">On <em data-td-invalid-detail="1" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;"> July 1, 2016, </em>the Company adopted ASU <em data-td-fact-id="34616670" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">2016</em>-<em data-td-fact-id="34616671" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">09,</em>&nbsp;Improvements to Employee Shared-Based Payment Accounting.&nbsp; Prior to the adoption of ASU <em data-td-fact-id="34616672" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">2019</em>-<em data-td-fact-id="34616673" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">09,</em> the Company had excess tax benefits for which benefits could <em data-td-fact-id="34616674" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">not</em> be previously recognized of approximately <em data-td-fact-id="34616675" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">$0.7</em> million, due to net operating loss carryforwards resulting from the windfall tax benefits.&nbsp; On <em data-td-invalid-detail="1" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;"> July 1, 2016, </em>upon the effective date of the adoption, the Company recognized the previously unrecognized excess tax benefits of <em data-td-fact-id="34616676" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">$0.7</em> million with an offsetting increase in the Company&rsquo;s valuation allowance using a modified retrospective method through a cumulative effect adjustment to the accumulated deficit, with <em data-td-fact-id="34616677" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">no</em> net impact on the Company&rsquo;s financial statements.</p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt 16.5pt;text-align:justify;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt 15pt;text-align:justify;">At <em data-td-invalid-detail="1" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;"> June 30, 2018, </em>the Company had net&nbsp;US deferred tax assets of approximately <em data-td-fact-id="34616678" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">$1.6</em> million. Due to uncertainties surrounding the Company&rsquo;s ability to generate future capital gains, a valuation allowance has been established to offset carry-forwards of its capital losses due to investments previously written off. Additionally, the future utilization of the Company&rsquo;s federal and state NOLs to offset future taxable income have been determined to be subject to annual limitation pursuant to Internal Revenue Code (&ldquo;IRC&rdquo;) Sections <em data-td-fact-id="34616679" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">382</em> and <em data-td-fact-id="34616680" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">383</em> as a result of ownership changes that have previously occurred.</p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt 15pt;text-align:center;text-indent:36pt;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt 15pt;text-align:justify;">Through its Section <em data-td-fact-id="34616681" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">382</em> study, the Company has analyzed any NOLs from its acquired subsidiaries to determine the maximum potential future tax benefit that might be available, and the corresponding limitation imposed based on IRC Section <em data-td-fact-id="34616682" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">382.</em> As a result, by the year ended <em data-td-invalid-detail="1" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;"> June 30, 2011, </em>the Company adjusted the aforementioned net operating losses previously estimated. The outcome resulted in a determination that it could utilize, annually, approximately <em data-td-fact-id="34616683" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">$0.4</em> million of previously incurred NOLs; presuming, however, there is taxable income in future periods affording utilization prior to expiration.</p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt 15pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:36pt;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt 15pt;text-align:justify;">At <em data-td-invalid-detail="1" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;"> June 30, 2018,&nbsp;</em>the Company had combined federal and state NOLs of approximately <em data-td-fact-id="34616684" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">$4.0</em> million and <em data-td-fact-id="34616685" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">$1.3</em> million, respectively.&nbsp; The federal and state tax loss carry-forwards will begin to expire in <em data-td-fact-id="34616686" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">2019</em> and <em data-td-fact-id="34616687" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">2024,</em> respectively, unless previously utilized.</p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt 15pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:36pt;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt 15pt;text-align:justify;">Significant components of the Company&rsquo;s net deferred tax assets at <em data-td-invalid-detail="1" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;"> June 30, 2018 </em>and <em data-td-fact-id="34616688" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">2017</em> are shown below. A valuation allowance of <em data-td-fact-id="34616689" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">$1.2</em> million and <em data-td-fact-id="34616690" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">$1.7</em> million has been established to offset the net deferred tax assets as of <em data-td-invalid-detail="1" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;"> June 30, 2018 </em>and <em data-td-fact-id="34616691" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">2017,</em> respectively. The net decrease in the valuation allowance of <em data-td-fact-id="34616692" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">$3.9</em> million&nbsp;for the year ended <em data-td-invalid-detail="1" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;"> June 30, 2017 </em>is primarily attributable to the partial release of the valuation allowance during the <em data-td-fact-id="34616693" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">three</em> months ended <em data-td-invalid-detail="1" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;"> June 30, 2017. </em>The Company released the valuation allowance on all of its domestic deferred tax assets, except for capital loss carry-forwards that are <em data-td-fact-id="34616694" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">not</em> more likely than <em data-td-fact-id="34616695" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">not</em> to be realized. The net decrease in the valuation allowance for the year ended <em data-td-invalid-detail="1" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;"> June 30, 2018 </em>was <em data-td-fact-id="34616696" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">$0.5</em> million, related to the change in federal tax rate discussed below.</p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt 15pt;text-align:justify;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt 15pt;text-align:left;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt 15pt;text-align:justify;">A provision had&nbsp;<em data-td-fact-id="34616700" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">not</em> been made at <em data-td-invalid-detail="1" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;"> June 30,</em>&nbsp;<em data-td-fact-id="34616701" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">2017,</em> for US for additional foreign withholding taxes on undistributed earnings of its UK subsidiaries because it was intention of management to reinvest the undistributed earnings indefinitely in foreign operations. Generally, such earnings become subject to U.S. tax upon the remittance of dividends and under certain other circumstances. It is <em data-td-fact-id="34616702" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">not</em> practicable to estimate the amount of deferred tax liability on such undistributed earnings.&nbsp; On <em data-td-invalid-detail="1" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;"> December 22, 2017, </em>new U.S. federal tax legislation, the Tax Cuts and Jobs Act (the &quot;Tax Act&quot;) was enacted. The Tax Act significantly revises the U.S corporate tax by implementing a territorial system and imposing a repatriation on deemed repatriated earnings of foreign subsidiaries. The Company derived that the enactment of the Tax Act&nbsp;will result in a tax of approximately <em data-td-fact-id="34616703" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">$0.2</em> million.</p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt 15pt;text-align:justify;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt 15pt;text-align:justify;">The Tax Act&nbsp;was a significant modification of existing U.S. federal tax law and contained several provisions which impacted the provision of the Company in fiscal year end <em data-td-invalid-detail="1" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;"> June 30, 2018 </em>and will impact the Company&#39;s tax position in future years. Among other things, the Tax Act permanently lowered the federal corporate tax rate to <em data-td-fact-id="34616704" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">21%</em> from the existing maximum tax rate of <em data-td-fact-id="34616705" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">35%,</em> effective for years including or commencing <em data-td-invalid-detail="1" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;"> January 1, 2018. </em>Due to the Company&#39;s fiscal year ending <em data-td-invalid-detail="1" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;"> June 30, 2018, </em>the federal tax rate is adjusted on a per-day computation based on the number of days in <em data-td-fact-id="34616706" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">2017</em> and <em data-td-fact-id="34616707" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">2018</em> with the old and new federal tax rates (the &quot;blended tax rate&quot;). For the fiscal year ended June <em data-td-fact-id="34616708" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">30,</em> <em data-td-fact-id="34616709" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">2018,</em> the Company recorded tax expense of approximately <em data-td-fact-id="34616710" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">$0.8</em>&nbsp;million primarily due to the remeasurement of deferred tax assets at the reduced federal corporate&nbsp;tax rate of <em data-td-fact-id="34616711" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">21%.</em></p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt 15pt;text-align:justify;"><br>
&nbsp;</p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt 15pt;text-align:justify;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt 15pt;text-align:justify;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt 15pt;text-align:center;">F-<em data-td-fact-id="34616712" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">18</em></p>

<div data-thunderdome-xbrl-exclude="1" id="PGBK" style="width: 100%; margin-left: 0pt; margin-right: 0pt">
<div id="PGNUM" style="text-align: center; width: 100%">&nbsp;</div>

<hr style="PAGE-BREAK-AFTER: always; border: none; width: 100%; height: 2px; color: #000000; background-color: #000000">
<div id="PGHDR" style="text-align: left; width: 100%">&nbsp;</div>
</div>

<p style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt 15pt;text-align:justify;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt 15pt;text-align:justify;">Beginning for tax years starting after <em data-td-invalid-detail="1" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;"> December 31, 2017, </em>the Tax Act eliminates the previous net operating loss carryback period of <em data-td-fact-id="34616713" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">two</em> years and permits an indefinite carryforward period. The net operating loss deduction is limited to <em data-td-fact-id="34616714" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">80%</em> of taxable income. The net operating losses arising in tax years beginning on or after <em data-td-invalid-detail="1" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;"> January 1, 2018 </em>are subject to the <em data-td-fact-id="34616715" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">80%</em> limitations. The net operating losses arising in tax years beginning before <em data-td-invalid-detail="1" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;"> January 1, 2018 </em>are <em data-td-fact-id="34616716" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">not</em> subject to the <em data-td-fact-id="34616717" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">80%</em> limitation. The net operating losses arising in tax years ending after <em data-td-invalid-detail="1" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;"> December 31, 2017 </em><em data-td-invalid-detail="1" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;"> may </em><em data-td-fact-id="34616718" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">not</em> be carried back to prior years and <em data-td-invalid-detail="1" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;"> may </em>be carried forward indefinitely.</p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt 15pt;text-align:justify;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt 15pt;text-align:justify;">For tax years commencing after <em data-td-invalid-detail="1" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;"> December 31, 2017, </em>the Tax Act repealed the alternative minimum tax and taxpayers with alternative minimum tax credit carryfowards that have <em data-td-fact-id="34616719" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">not</em> been used <em data-td-invalid-detail="1" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;"> may </em>claim a refund in future years for those credits even though <em data-td-fact-id="34616720" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">no</em> income tax liabilities exist. Business expense deductions are eliminated for most entertainment costs and commuting benefits. Certain employer-provided meals expenses will also be eliminated after the year <em data-td-fact-id="34616721" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">2025.</em> The bonus depreciation expensing provision increased from <em data-td-fact-id="34616722" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">50%</em> to <em data-td-fact-id="34616723" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">100%</em> for assets placed in service after <em data-td-invalid-detail="1" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;"> September 27, 2018 </em>and before <em data-td-fact-id="34616724" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">2023.</em></p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt 15pt;text-align:justify;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt 15pt;text-align:justify;">The Tax Act also subjects U.S. corporations to tax on Global Intangible Low-Taxed Income (&ldquo;GILTI&rdquo;), which imposes tax on foreign earnings in excess of a deemed return on tangible assets. Due to the complexity of the new GILTI tax rules, the Company is continuing to evaluate this provision for which&nbsp;<em data-td-fact-id="34616725" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">no</em>&nbsp;provisional amounts have been recorded in the Company&rsquo;s Consolidated Financial Statements. An accounting policy election can be made to either record deferred taxes related to GILTI or to record the related taxes in the period in which they occur. The Company has <em data-td-fact-id="34616726" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">not</em> yet elected an accounting policy related to GILTI and will only do so after completion of further evaluation and analysis. The provisions related to GILTI are subject to adjustment during the measurement period ending <em data-td-invalid-detail="1" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;"> December 2018.</em></p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt 15pt;text-align:justify;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt 15pt;text-align:justify;">In addition, the Tax Act substantially eliminates any element of deferred taxation of foreign income with a US parented multinational group and retains Subpart F income to provide full and immediate taxation of the classes of income under the pre-enactment law and subjects a new broad class of income under Subpart F as well creates new base erosion provisions.</p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt 15pt;text-align:justify;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt 15pt;text-align:justify;">&nbsp;</p>
</div>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt 15pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:36pt;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt 15pt;text-align:justify;"><b>Legal Matters</b></p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt 15pt;text-align:justify;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt 15pt;text-align:justify;">From time to time, the Company is subject to various legal claims and proceedings arising in the ordinary course of business. The ultimate disposition of such a proceeding if initiated could have material adverse effects on the consolidated financial position or results of operations of the Company. There are currently <em data-td-fact-id="34616728" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">no</em> pending material legal proceedings.</p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt 15pt;text-align:justify;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt 15pt;text-align:justify;"><b>Indemnities and Guarantees</b></p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt 15pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:36pt;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt 15pt;text-align:justify;">The Company has made certain indemnities and guarantees, under which it <em data-td-invalid-detail="1" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;"> may </em>be required to make payments to a guaranteed or indemnified party, in relation to certain actions or transactions. The Company indemnifies its directors, officers, employees and agents, as permitted under the laws of the State of Delaware. In connection with its&nbsp;Credit Facility (see Note <em data-td-fact-id="34616729" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">4</em>), the Company indemnified the lender for certain losses, claims, and other liabilities that are standard for this type of agreement. In connection with its facility leases, the Company has indemnified its lessors for certain claims arising from the use of the facilities. In connection with its customers&rsquo; contracts the Company indemnifies the customer that the software provided does <em data-td-fact-id="34616730" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">not</em> violate any US patent. The duration of the guarantees and indemnities varies, and is generally tied to the life of the agreement. These guarantees and indemnities do <em data-td-fact-id="34616731" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">not</em> provide for any limitation of the maximum potential future payments the Company could be obligated to make. Historically, the Company has <em data-td-fact-id="34616732" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">not</em> been obligated to make nor incurred any payments for these obligations and, therefore, <em data-td-fact-id="34616733" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">no</em> liabilities have been recorded for these indemnities and guarantees in the accompanying consolidated balance sheets.</p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt 15pt;text-align:justify;">&nbsp;&nbsp;<b>&nbsp;</b></p>
